svg.title: Vulkan versus ROCm in fak: the portability-versus-tuning trade, the two paths that pay the per-op tax in different places, and the evidence ladder that separates what has been measured from what has only been declared
svg.desc: The comparison has three parts. First, the one-sentence difference: Vulkan is a cross-vendor standard specified by Khronos and implemented by every vendor's driver, so it runs on AMD, NVIDIA and Intel; ROCm is AMD's own native stack, so it runs on AMD only. That single fact generates the trade, drawn as a horizontal axis from portability on the left to tuning on the right: a cross-vendor API must present the intersection of what every vendor can implement, so it cannot expose AMD's 64-lane versus 32-lane wavefront distinction, while a native stack can expose everything the silicon has. Second, the two dispatch paths, which differ in where the per-operation cost is paid rather than in whether one is paid. The Vulkan path goes from a Go backend operation through cgo into internal/compute/vulkan_shim.cpp, records a command buffer, submits it with vkQueueSubmit and waits on a fence, and pays roughly 2 milliseconds per operation; the ROCm path goes from a Go backend operation through cgo into internal/compute/rocm_backend.go under the rocm build tag, makes a HIP runtime call that launches a kernel, and pays a launch cost instead, which the CUDA-on-WSL comparison on the same class of problem measures at roughly 0.07 milliseconds per operation. Both are single-stream first cuts: vulkanMu at internal/compute/vulkan.go:69 and rocmMu at internal/compute/rocm_backend.go:22 each serialize their whole backend, and both register in the Approx correctness class, at internal/compute/vulkan.go:587 and internal/compute/rocm_backend.go:62 respectively, graded against the cpu-ref Reference path. Third, the evidence ladder, which is the part that makes the comparison trustworthy: measured on silicon at the top, holding Vulkan's full forward pass on an RX 7600 with argmax-exact results, prefill cosine 1.0, roughly 2.5 tokens per second decode and the roughly 60 times gap behind llama.cpp; then host-witnessed, holding the pure-Go ROCm taxonomy that needs no GPU, ROCmFamily at internal/compute/rocm_arch.go:30, the rocmArches table at internal/compute/rocm_arch.go:105 and Datacenter at internal/compute/rocm_arch.go:92; then silicon-witnessed once, holding the 2026-09-10 correctness run on a gfx1151 part recorded at docs/tickets/native-rocm-backend/TICKET-01.md:64; and at the bottom declared but unmeasured, holding the ROCm throughput bar of within 1.5 times Vulkan, which is graded by WithinTarget at internal/compute/prefill.go:281 and has never been attempted, so no ROCm speed number exists at all.
svg.text: Vulkan vs ROCm — the trade, the two paths, and the evidence
One sentence generates everything below it: Vulkan is a cross-vendor standard, ROCm is one vendor's native stack.
1 · the trade — portability and tuning pull in opposite directions
PORTABILITY
TUNING
Vulkan — cross-vendor standard
specified by Khronos · implemented by every vendor's driver
runs on AMD, NVIDIA and Intel — one shader binary, re-targeted
the machine it presents is the INTERSECTION of what all have
so it cannot say "the wavefront is 64 lanes"
ROCm — AMD's native stack
AMD's compiler (hipcc), runtime and libraries · AMD only
the machine it presents is the SILICON, with nothing hidden
models 64-lane (GCN/CDNA) vs 32-lane (RDNA) wavefronts
rocm_arch.go:27 — the wrong family "silently mistunes occupancy and LDS"
The principle: portability is achieved by hiding the machine, and hiding the machine costs you the ability to tune for it.
2 · the two paths — both pay a per-op tax, in different places
VULKAN PATH
Go backend op → cgo → vulkan_shim.cpp
record a CommandBuffer (bind pipeline,
descriptors, push constants, dispatch)
vkQueueSubmit + fence wait → driver → GPU
~2 ms/op — paid in the DRIVER, per command buffer
vulkanMu (vulkan.go:69) · Class() = Approx (vulkan.go:587)
one serialized queue — no overlap of compute with transfer
ROCM PATH
Go backend op → cgo → rocm_backend.go
(//go:build linux && rocm && cgo)
HIP runtime call → hipLaunchKernel
kernel launch → GPU
~0.07 ms/op — paid in the RUNTIME, per launch
rocmMu (rocm_backend.go:22) · Class() = Approx (rocm_backend.go:62)
the 0.07 ms is the CUDA-on-WSL comparison, not a ROCm measurement
The paths differ in where the per-op cost is paid, not in whether one is paid. The bet is that a launch is far cheaper than a command-buffer round trip.
3 · the evidence ladder — the part that makes the comparison trustworthy
MEASURED ON SILICON — Vulkan: full forward on an RX 7600 (gfx1102), argmax-exact, prefill cosine 1.0, ~2.5 tok/s decode, ~60× behind llama.cpp
HOST-WITNESSED — ROCm: the pure-Go taxonomy, ROCmFamily (rocm_arch.go:30) · rocmArches (:105) · Datacenter() (:92) — unit-tested on any host, no GPU
SILICON-WITNESSED ONCE — ROCm: correctness only, 2026-09-10, HIP 7.2, gfx1151, required-device tests passing with no skips (TICKET-01.md:64)
DECLARED, UNMEASURED — ROCm: "within 1.5× Vulkan throughput", graded by WithinTarget (prefill.go:281) — never attempted; no ROCm speed number exists
